name: site-architecture
description: Plan site structure and information architecture for a website: a page tree where every page has exactly one parent, URL rules, navigation labels and breadcrumbs; an internal linking plan from a links export (source and target) that uses only your own URLs, with inlinks and click depth before and after; hub page and child page links; which filter URLs get indexable pages, with the URL count worked out; and a redirect map for site migrations and URL changes, checked for chains, loops and homepage targets. Not a search audit and not software architecture.

interface.longDescription: Five skills for planning how a website is organised; each answers the question you asked first, in a form a web team can build. Information architecture turns a page list, menus or a site description into a tree where every page has one parent, with URL rules, navigation and breadcrumbs and the list of URLs that move, as far as you ask for them. The internal linking plan reads a links export, computes click depth and inlinks, proposes new links that use only URLs found in your data (the most useful 30 or so first when you give no number), and shows what the edits change. Hub design wires one topic's pages into a hub with child pages. Facet policy counts the URLs your filters can create and decides which may be crawled and indexed, with a robots.txt and noindex conflict check. The site migration redirect map builds or checks a map for chains, loops, homepage targets and temporary codes, and gives a launch checklist when you ask. The plugin gives no traffic forecasts. It reads what you paste and, in information architecture only, if you name your own site and your assistant has a web tool, its robots.txt, up to three sitemaps and up to five public pages. It changes nothing on your site.
defaultPrompt: Laptop filters, single-select: brand 8, RAM 4, GPU 6, screen 5, price 6. How many filter URLs, and which to index?
Plan the URL tree for a B2B SaaS site: 6 features, 40 integrations, blog, docs, pricing. One parent per page; nav spec.
